title: The finite-kernel criterion for equal-dimensional abelian varieties
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $A,B$ be abelian varieties over $k$ [def-sc-abelian-variety], and let $f:A\to B$ be a homomorphism of $k$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme]. Suppose $\dim A=\dim B$ [def-pc-dimension] and the scheme-theoretic kernel $\ker f=A\times_{B,f,e_B}\operatorname{Spec}k$ is finite over $k$, in the sense of [def-sc-group-scheme]. Then $f$ is surjective and finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free].

source.place: Chapter I Proposition 7.1(c) implies (d), printed p.32; finite local freeness is the locally free conclusion in its proof. Equivalently Stacks Project, Morphisms, Tag 02KB, lemma-finite-flat, literature/stacks-project/morphisms.tex, identifies finite flat morphisms over a locally Noetherian target with finite locally free morphisms.

proof.text: By [def-sc-abelian-variety] and [def-weil-proper-morphism], $A$ is proper and $B$ is separated, both of finite type over $k$. Apply [pqf-lem-image-proper] over $\operatorname{Spec}k$: the scheme-theoretic image $i:Z\hookrightarrow B$ is closed and proper over $k$, and $f=i\circ g$ with $g:A\to Z$ proper and surjective. By [lem-sc-abelian-variety-characterization], $B$ is irreducible. These schemes are nonempty, since the identity of $A$ maps into $Z$.

source.place: Chapter I Proposition 7.1, proof, printed p.32

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-kernel-group-fibres] to $f$. Every scheme fibre $A_b$ has dimension at most zero. The same holds for every fibre of $g$: a closed immersion identifies the residue fields at $z$ and $i(z)$, and $A\times_Z\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(z)=A\times_B\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(i(z))$ by the fibre-product universal property. Thus all fibres of $g$ have dimension at most zero.

source.place: Chapter I Proposition 7.1, proof, printed p.32

proof.text: Use [lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings] to read the given dimensions as topological Krull dimensions. They are finite by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]. Since $Z$ is a nonempty closed subspace of $B$, inclusion of chains gives $0\leq\dim Z\leq\dim B<\infty$. Apply [lem-zl-finite-type-fibre-image-dimension-bounds] to $g:A\to Z$, with $d=\dim Z$ and fibre bound $n=0$, obtaining $\dim A\leq\dim Z$. If $Z\neq B$ as a closed subset, append the irreducible closed subset $B$ to every strict chain of nonempty irreducible closed subsets of $Z$. Each remains closed in $B$, so $\dim Z+1\leq\dim B$. This contradicts $\dim A=\dim B$ and $\dim A\leq\dim Z$. Hence $i(Z)=B$ topologically, and surjectivity of $g$ proves surjectivity of $f$. No equality of closed subschemes is needed.

source.place: Chapter I Proposition 7.1, proof, printed p.32

proof.text: The surjectivity just proved and the given finite scheme-theoretic kernel make $f$ an isogeny by [def-sc-isogeny]. Apply [lem-sc-isogeny-degree]: $f$ is finite and flat, and $f_*\mathcal O_A$ is locally free of rank equal to the order of the kernel.

source.place: Chapter I Proposition 7.1, proof, printed p.32

proof.text: The scheme $B$ is locally Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since it is of finite type over the spectrum of the field $k$. The finite morphism $f$ is locally of finite type: finite module generators of an affine section algebra also generate it as an algebra. Therefore [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth] makes $f$ locally of finite presentation. Together with finite and flat from Step 4, this is exactly finite local freeness in [def-pc-finite-locally-free].

Step 5: B is Noetherian, finite implies locally of finite type, which gives locally finite presentation by pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth; that is def-pc-finite-locally-free verbatim.
